title: The Lawn Debate: Abolition vs. Preservation
description: A complete debate map of arguments for and against residential lawns in America

participants.name: abolitionist
participants.position: Lawns should be abolished through policy and social change

participants.name: preservationist
participants.position: Lawns provide value and should remain

facts.assertion: US lawn irrigation consumes 2.9 trillion gallons annually
Lawn irrigation is 8-9 billion gallons per day
US public water supply is ~39 billion gallons per day
50% of lawn irrigation water is wasted through evaporation and runoff
US lawn coverage is approximately 40 million acres
facts.source: Milesi et al. (2005), NASA/UCSB satellite data

facts.assertion: All US vegetables occupy roughly 4 million acres harvested
Lawns are monocultures that support minimal insect and wildlife life
Lawns receive 3-9x more pesticide per acre than agricultural crops
~45-49 million Americans live under HOA lawn governance
Hundreds of municipalities have weed ordinances classifying unmowed grass as public nuisance
US landscaping industry revenue is ~$153 billion annually (2024)
facts.source: IBIS World / National Association of Landscape Professionals

facts.assertion: Water and sewer rates have risen 24% over five years
50-70% of summer water bills go to lawn irrigation
US data centers consume 17 billion gallons of water annually
Lawn water use is 170x greater than all US data centers

stasis_candidates.point: Do lawns provide net benefit or net harm to society?
Are lawns a matter of individual choice or system enforcement?
Can water conservation and lawn maintenance coexist?
